name: Kukna
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Chaudhari, Vikram G. 2009. Chaudhari, Dhodiya, Gamit ane Kunkana bhasha: ek abhyas [Chaudhari, Dhodia, Gamit and Kunkna languages: a study]. PhD thesis (in Gujarati), Department of Gujarati, Veer Narmad South Gujarat University, Surat (guide J. M. Gurjar). 314 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/324098. Chapters 1-7 + bibliography fetched sources; ch.4 scanned (tesseract guj+eng).
sources.note: Ch.4 'svar-vyanjan' (pp.123-177) gives vowel and consonant inventories and Gujarati-to-Kunkna sound correspondences (4.8 Kunkna vowels p.141; 4.12 Kunkna consonants pp.168-170). No statement of where word stress falls. Nearest remark, p.141: 'કુંકણામાં અ, આ, એ, ઍ, ઓ, ઑ, ઇ, ઈ, ઉ, ઊ, (અ̭) (સ્વર ભારાંક માટે વપરાય છે. સાદા સ્વર કરતાં વધારે ભાર મૂકી ઉચ્ચારાય તો જ તેનો અર્થ થાય) કુલ અગિયાર સ્વર જોવા મળે છે.' sources.citation: Kavadi, Naresh Bhikaji. 1954. Folk-songs from Dang: a linguistic study (with comparative reference to Dangi as spoken today). PhD thesis, University of Poona / Deccan College (guide S. G. Tulpule). 833 pp. In English. Shodhganga hdl 10603/174921 (title, contents, abbreviations, bibliography, Part I Introduction, Part II Phonology fetched sources; Parts III-V and appendices not fetched sources).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Historical (Bloch/Turner-style) phonology of the language of Dangs folk-songs (DFS, secs.26-193) and of Modern Dangi (secs.194-302); no section on accent and no general stress rule. Only incidental remark, Part II sec.78, p.139: 'In the following cases the stress on the first syllable has given rise to the diphthong ai. e.g. बैरम (ब्रह्म); मैतर, मैत्तढ (मित्र); सैहर (फा. शहर); स्वैंवर (स्वयंवर).' (summarised again Part I sec.9 p.61). NB Dangi = areal speech of the Dangs (Bhils, Konkanas/Kunbis = Kukna, Varlis), which Glottolog

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India (gen. supervision S. S. Bhattacharya & S. P. Ahirwal; investigation & report M. K. Koul & Ranjita Pattanayak). 2003 [pr. 2004]. Linguistic Survey of India, Special Studies: Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Kolkata: ORGI Language Division. 101 pp. scan (no text layer; tesseract scanned of PDF pp.13-60 saved).
sources.note: Nothing for Kukna. The volume's grammar (Phonology pp.32-46, Morphology, Syntax) is of Varli only; Kokna/Kokni/Kukna figures only in the sociolinguistic introduction (classed under Bhili/Bhilodi with Varli and Dhodia; 'Konkani (Bhili)' of the 1961 census = Kokna/Kokni/Kukna, p.27 of print) and in the Comparative Vocabulary List pp.80-87 (Ahirwal). Even for Varli the suprasegmentals listed are only 'Nasalisation and length' (p.32, p.34); the words stress/accent do not occur in the phonology.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part III: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia &c. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Konkani' [the Bhil 'Konkani' of Nawsari, Dharampur, Bansda, Surgana, Nasik (Peint, Kalwan) and Khandesh = Kukna], pp.130 ff.
sources.note: Nothing. The Konkani (Bhil) notes mention only nasalisation of vowels and mixed Gujarati-Bhili/Marathi inflexion; the only 'accent' in the volume is the transcription convention in the front matter (acute marks an accented syllable when needed), never applied to this dialect.

sources.citation: Hammarström et al. Glottolog 5.1, languoid page 'Kukna' kukn1238 (bookkeeping) and 'Dhodia-Kukna' dhod1238; local copy of glottolog-cldf-5.1 sources.bib searched for [kex]/[dho]/Dangs/Kokna/Varli entries.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Comment: 'Kukna [kex] is listed in E16-E28 as a separate language but the Kukna speak a language intelligible to that in the Dhodia [dho] entry' (refs Ahirwal 2003; Ethnologue). Descriptive refs for dho/kex are only Grierson 1907, Ahirwal 2003 wordlist, ethnographies; n_glottolog_desc_refs for kukn1238 = 0.
